input.prompt:
Read-only analysis. Repo: ~/scratch-relai/bench/relai-p2 (a snapshot of gpt-researcher, an LLM web-research agent that writes cited reports). Do not edit any files.

Goal: find where the CORE research agent is likely to fail for its users — wrong/uncited/hallucinated reports, silent degradation, wrong report type/length/language, broken citations, crashes on realistic inputs, cost blowups, prompt-injection from scraped pages, etc. Scope: gpt_researcher/agent.py, gpt_researcher/prompts.py, gpt_researcher/actions/*, gpt_researcher/skills/* (researcher, writer, curator, context_manager, deep_research, browser), gpt_researcher/context/*, gpt_researcher/utils/llm.py, gpt_researcher/config/* (defaults), gpt_researcher/memory/embeddings.py. Read the actual code and prompt text; file names are not evidence.

For each candidate risk report: (a) mechanism (what code/prompt does), (b) realistic trigger, (c) observable failure for the user, (d) evidence as file:line with a SHORT quote (≤2 lines), (e) your confidence (high/med/low) and impact (high/med/low). Prefer risks where code allows what a prompt only asks against, where errors are swallowed and the run continues with empty/degraded context, where LLM output is parsed fragilely, where prompts contradict each other or config, and where prompts state requirements (citation format, language, word count, date awareness, source usage) that code doesn't enforce. Also list the explicit behavioral requirements stated in prompts (with file:line) — these are what the agent promises users. Also note any ambiguities/contradictions as open questions. Aim for ~10-20 well-evidenced risks, no filler. Keep the final report under ~1800 words.

input.command: cd ~/scratch-relai/bench/relai-p2/gpt_researcher; wc -l agent.py prompts.py actions/*.py skills/*.py context/*.py utils/llm.py config/*.py memory/embeddings.py
